difficultyReason: Two-step causal chain (new drug → reduced inflammation → improved outcomes). The weakener attacks the move from the clinical evidence to the conclusion by introducing a confound at the second link. One distractor strengthens, one is out-of-scope.
stimulus: Researchers at a teaching hospital administered a new anti-inflammatory drug to patients recovering from knee replacement surgery. Those patients showed measurably lower inflammation markers over the following two weeks and also reported significantly less post-operative pain than patients who received a standard pain regimen. The researchers concluded that the drug's anti-inflammatory action was responsible for the reduction in reported pain.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the researchers' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new drug contains an opioid compound that directly suppresses pain signals in the central nervous system, independent of any anti-inflammatory effect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients who received the new drug were more likely to follow the prescribed physical therapy regimen than those who received the standard pain regimen.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inflammation markers measured in blood plasma are a reliable proxy for tissue-level inflammation in post-surgical patients.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The standard pain regimen used in the comparison group has been in clinical use for more than two decades.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Patients who reported less pain during recovery also tended to have shorter hospital stays.

explanations.correct: The researchers claim the drug works through its anti-inflammatory action. If the drug contains a compound that directly suppresses pain independently of inflammation, the pain reduction could be explained by that mechanism rather than anti-inflammation — directly undermining the causal claim.
explanations.A: Correct. Introduces an alternative causal mechanism that explains pain reduction without invoking anti-inflammatory action, severing the link the researchers depend on.
explanations.B: Shifts subject — this would weaken the conclusion that the drug itself caused pain reduction, but it attacks a different causal path (therapy compliance) rather than the anti-inflammatory mechanism specifically claimed. Slightly relevant but weaker than A.
explanations.C: Strengthens. Validates the measurement tool the researchers used, bolstering the evidence that inflammation was actually reduced.
explanations.D: Out-of-scope. The longevity of the standard regimen's clinical use has no bearing on the mechanism by which the new drug reduces pain.
explanations.E: Accurate but irrelevant — the correlation between pain and hospital stay duration does not speak to whether anti-inflammation caused pain reduction.

difficultyReason: Predictive argument: economist predicts a policy outcome based on historical analogy. The weakener attacks the disanalogy between the historical case and the present one. Distractors include one that strengthens the analogy and one that is narrowly about a different time period.
stimulus: An economist argues that imposing a modest tariff on imported steel will revitalize domestic steel production, pointing to a 1980s tariff that was followed by a 10 percent increase in domestic steel output within three years. Because the current tariff proposal mirrors the 1980s measure in both rate and scope, the economist predicts a comparable increase in output will follow its enactment.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the economist's prediction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Unlike in the 1980s, most domestic manufacturers today rely on imported steel components that would become significantly more expensive under the proposed tariff, reducing their demand for domestic steel.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The 1980s tariff was accompanied by a simultaneous government subsidy program for domestic steel producers that is not part of the current proposal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Steel output in several competing nations increased substantially during the years following the 1980s tariff.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The current tariff proposal has received bipartisan support in both legislative chambers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Domestic steel production has declined steadily over the past decade, reaching its lowest level in forty years.

explanations.correct: The economist's analogy depends on the two situations being sufficiently similar. If the 1980s tariff was accompanied by a subsidy program absent from the current proposal, the output increase may have been driven by the subsidy rather than (or in addition to) the tariff — breaking the analogy and undermining the prediction.
explanations.A: Plausible weakener, but it introduces a new mechanism (downstream demand reduction) rather than directly attacking the historical analogy the argument rests on. B more precisely targets the premise that the two situations are comparable.
explanations.B: Correct. Identifies a critical disanalogy — a confounding policy present in the historical case but absent now — that explains the earlier output increase and severs the analogical basis for the prediction.
explanations.C: Out-of-scope. Foreign output levels during the 1980s don't bear on whether a similar domestic tariff today will yield a similar domestic output increase.
explanations.D: Irrelevant to the economic prediction — political support says nothing about the causal mechanism or likely outcome.
explanations.E: This might seem to strengthen concern about domestic production but actually could support the tariff's rationale. It does not weaken the argument that the tariff will produce an increase comparable to the 1980s.

difficultyReason: Causal argument from correlation in an environmental science context. The conclusion overreaches by declaring a pollutant the cause of declining amphibian populations. The weakener introduces an alternative explanation; distractors include a strengthener and a premise-only attacker.
stimulus: A wildlife biologist documented a sharp decline in spotted salamander populations in wetlands located near an agricultural region where atrazine use has increased markedly over the past fifteen years. Water samples from those wetlands contained atrazine concentrations above levels shown in laboratory studies to impair amphibian reproduction. The biologist concluded that atrazine runoff is causing the population decline.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the biologist's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Spotted salamander populations in wetlands far from agricultural activity have remained stable over the same fifteen-year period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The wetlands near the agricultural region also border a highway whose construction over the past fifteen years has significantly reduced the surrounding forest habitat on which spotted salamanders depend for breeding migration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Atrazine has been shown to cause hormonal disruption in multiple amphibian species in addition to spotted salamanders.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Laboratory studies establishing the reproductive impairment threshold for atrazine used juvenile salamanders, whereas the biologist's field samples measured adult populations.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Farmers in the agricultural region have begun voluntarily reducing atrazine application rates in response to environmental concerns.

explanations.correct: The biologist concludes atrazine caused the decline. If a major habitat disruption (highway construction reducing breeding forest) occurred simultaneously in the same area, that provides an alternative explanation for the population decline, seriously undermining the causal conclusion.
explanations.A: This actually strengthens the argument by providing a control-group comparison suggesting the decline is specific to atrazine-exposed wetlands.
explanations.B: Correct. Introduces a competing causal factor — habitat loss due to highway construction — that could independently explain the observed population decline, weakening the conclusion that atrazine is the cause.
explanations.C: Strengthens. Broadens the evidence that atrazine is harmful to amphibians, supporting the biologist's causal claim.
explanations.D: Attacks a premise (the relevance of laboratory threshold data) without fully undermining the conclusion — the field concentrations could still be causing harm even if the lab data is imperfect. This is the 'too narrow' trap.
explanations.E: Irrelevant to whether atrazine caused the past and ongoing decline; future reduction in application rates does not address the causal claim.

difficultyReason: Policy argument predicting that a legal change will reduce a harmful outcome. The weakener shows the mechanism connecting the policy to the outcome is unreliable. One distractor is an opposite answer (strengthens); one is out-of-scope.
stimulus: A state legislature is debating a bill that would mandate a minimum three-day waiting period before any firearm purchase is finalized. Proponents point to studies showing that a significant proportion of gun-related suicides involve firearms purchased within 24 hours of the act. They conclude that the waiting period will meaningfully reduce the state's gun-related suicide rate.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument for the waiting period's effectiveness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most individuals who attempt suicide using a recently purchased firearm have no prior history of diagnosed mental illness.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The state already has among the highest rates of household firearm ownership in the country, meaning most residents at risk already have access to a firearm in the home.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Waiting periods for firearm purchases have been adopted in several other states over the past two decades.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Suicidal crises frequently intensify over periods longer than three days, so a waiting period would not eliminate risk.

choices.label: E
choices.text: States that have implemented waiting periods have recorded lower rates of gun-related suicides than states without such policies.

explanations.correct: The argument assumes the waiting period will reduce access to firearms at the moment of crisis. If most at-risk residents already own a firearm, the waiting period on new purchases would not meaningfully restrict access, breaking the link between the policy and the predicted reduction in suicides.
explanations.A: Irrelevant to the mechanism by which the waiting period would or would not work — prior mental illness history does not bear on firearm access at time of crisis.
explanations.B: Correct. Undermines the mechanism: if at-risk individuals already possess firearms, delaying new purchases does not reduce their access, severing the causal link between the policy and the predicted outcome.
explanations.C: Out-of-scope. The fact that other states have adopted waiting periods says nothing about whether this state's waiting period will be effective.
explanations.D: This is the 'too narrow' / straw-man trap. It attacks a stronger version of the conclusion (complete elimination of risk) rather than the actual conclusion (meaningful reduction). The argument only claims a meaningful reduction, not elimination.
explanations.E: Strengthens. Provides empirical evidence that waiting periods correlate with lower suicide rates, directly supporting the conclusion.

difficultyReason: Argument from historical evidence to a conclusion about technological causation. The weakener is a classic reverse-causation / confound attack. Distractors include one that strengthens and one that attacks an irrelevant adjacent claim.
stimulus: A technology historian argues that the widespread adoption of the printing press in fifteenth-century Europe directly caused the rapid spread of Protestant ideas during the Reformation. As evidence, the historian cites the fact that the regions where printing presses were most densely concentrated also experienced the earliest and most extensive Protestant conversions.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most calls into question the historian's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Protestant reformers were among the earliest and most prolific users of the printing press to disseminate their theological texts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The regions with the highest concentration of printing presses in fifteenth-century Europe were also major commercial centers whose populations had higher literacy rates and greater exposure to new ideas through trade networks, independent of printed materials.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Several regions with few printing presses eventually adopted Protestant ideas after prolonged exposure to traveling preachers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Catholic Church attempted to restrict the distribution of Protestant pamphlets produced by printing presses in several regions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Martin Luther's Ninety-Five Theses were among the most widely printed documents of the early sixteenth century.

explanations.correct: The historian infers causation from the correlation between press density and Protestant conversion. B introduces a confounding variable — high literacy and trade-network exposure in commercial centers — that could explain both the concentration of presses and the spread of Protestant ideas, without the press being the cause.
explanations.A: Strengthens. Confirms that reformers actively used the press to spread ideas, supporting the causal claim.
explanations.B: Correct. Identifies a common cause (commercial center characteristics) that explains both variables, undermining the inference that press density caused Protestant conversion.
explanations.C: This is the 'too narrow' trap. It shows the press wasn't strictly necessary, but does not undermine the claim that the press caused early and extensive conversion in press-dense regions.
explanations.D: Irrelevant to whether the press caused conversions; Church resistance would, if anything, suggest the press was effective (consistent with the historian's view).
explanations.E: Strengthens, or at minimum is irrelevant. Confirming Luther's texts were widely printed is consistent with the historian's causal claim.

difficultyReason: Ethics/policy argument where the conclusion generalizes from one sample to a broader population. The weakener attacks the representativeness of the sample. Distractors include one strengthener and one that addresses an irrelevant demographic.
stimulus: A nonprofit organization surveyed 600 adults in a large metropolitan area and found that 74 percent supported a proposed city ordinance requiring restaurants to display letter grades for food safety inspections. Citing these results, the organization concluded that the ordinance has broad public support and urged the city council to enact it without delay.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the organization's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The survey was conducted exclusively at farmers' markets and organic grocery stores, venues whose patrons tend to have unusually strong preferences for food transparency regulations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Similar letter-grading ordinances in other cities have been shown to improve restaurant hygiene compliance rates within two years of enactment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A majority of restaurant owners in the city oppose the proposed ordinance on the grounds that it unfairly penalizes establishments for minor infractions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The survey question was phrased to clearly distinguish the proposed letter-grade system from a numerical scoring system that had previously been rejected.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Seventy-four percent support among survey respondents exceeds the two-thirds threshold that city council typically requires before advancing major ordinances.

explanations.correct: The conclusion claims the ordinance has broad public support, but if the survey was conducted only at venues with self-selected, atypically food-transparency-conscious patrons, the sample is unrepresentative of the general public — directly undermining the generalization.
explanations.A: Correct. Attacks the representativeness of the sample, revealing selection bias that invalidates the inference from survey results to broad public support.
explanations.B: Out-of-scope. The effectiveness of the ordinance in other cities is irrelevant to whether this city's public broadly supports the proposed ordinance.
explanations.C: Shift in subject. Restaurant owners' opposition is a different constituency from the general public; the argument is about public (resident) support, not business-owner support.
explanations.D: Strengthens. Suggests the survey methodology was careful and results are not an artifact of question framing.
explanations.E: Strengthens. Suggests the measured support exceeds the practical threshold for council action, bolstering the case for enactment.

difficultyReason: Causal argument in linguistics concluding that bilingual education causes improved cognitive outcomes. The weakener introduces a selection-effect confound. One distractor attacks a different link in the chain; one strengthens.
stimulus: A school district compared standardized cognitive-flexibility test scores for students enrolled in its bilingual immersion program with scores for students in its standard monolingual curriculum. The bilingual students scored, on average, 18 percent higher on the cognitive-flexibility measures. District administrators concluded that participation in the bilingual program is responsible for the students' superior cognitive-flexibility scores.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the administrators' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enrollment in the bilingual program requires a written application, and admitted students are disproportionately drawn from households where parents have higher levels of education and place a strong emphasis on academic achievement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cognitive-flexibility tests used by the district have been validated in multiple peer-reviewed studies as reliable measures of executive function in school-age children.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students in the bilingual program spend more hours per week on structured classroom tasks than students in the standard curriculum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cognitive-flexibility scores tend to improve naturally as children age, regardless of the curriculum they follow.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Several peer-reviewed studies conducted in other countries have found a positive association between bilingualism and cognitive-flexibility measures.

explanations.correct: The conclusion attributes the score difference to the bilingual program. If enrollment is selective in a way that admits students from academically oriented households, those students may have higher cognitive-flexibility scores due to home environment rather than the program — a classic selection-effect confound that undermines the causal inference.
explanations.A: Correct. Reveals a selection bias: the bilingual group may be cognitively advantaged before the program begins due to socioeconomic and parental factors, not because of the program itself.
explanations.B: Strengthens. Validates the measurement instrument, bolstering confidence in the score difference as a real effect.
explanations.C: This is a 'too narrow' trap — it introduces an alternative explanation (instructional time) but leaves open whether that instructional time is part of what 'bilingual program participation' means. It weakens marginally but less decisively than A.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — if both groups aged equally over the study period, natural developmental improvement would not explain the difference between groups.
explanations.E: Strengthens. External evidence supports the causal claim that bilingualism improves cognitive flexibility.

difficultyReason: Predictive argument in technology policy where the conclusion forecasts reduced energy consumption from a software update. The weakener attacks the move from lab-measured efficiency gains to real-world consumption outcomes (rebound effect). Distractors include one out-of-scope and one strengthener.
stimulus: An electronics manufacturer announced that a firmware update for its line of smart televisions reduces the power draw of each unit by 22 percent during active use. The manufacturer concluded that when owners install the update, total electricity consumption attributable to the company's televisions will decrease substantially.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the manufacturer's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The firmware update also improves picture quality, which many users have cited as a reason to increase the number of hours per day they use their televisions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The 22 percent reduction in power draw was measured in laboratory conditions that closely replicate average household viewing environments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Smart televisions account for a growing share of residential electricity consumption relative to other consumer electronics.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The manufacturer's televisions are sold in over forty countries, each with different residential electricity pricing structures.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Other electronics manufacturers have released similar energy-efficiency updates for their smart televisions in the same period.

explanations.correct: Even if each unit draws 22 percent less power per hour, total consumption depends on total hours used. If improved picture quality causes users to watch significantly more hours, overall electricity consumption may not decrease — this is a rebound-effect weakener that attacks the inference from per-unit efficiency to aggregate consumption.
explanations.A: Correct. Introduces the rebound effect: the efficiency gain per hour of use may be offset by increased usage hours, undermining the conclusion that total consumption will decrease substantially.
explanations.B: Strengthens. Validates the per-unit efficiency figure by confirming lab conditions were realistic, supporting the premise from which the conclusion is drawn.
explanations.C: Irrelevant to whether the firmware update causes a decrease; this describes a trend independent of the update's effect.
explanations.D: Out-of-scope. Pricing structures affect consumer behavior but are too remote from the causal chain to undermine the conclusion as directly as A.
explanations.E: Shift in subject — other manufacturers' updates don't bear on whether this manufacturer's update will reduce consumption of this company's televisions.

difficultyReason: Legal reasoning argument where an attorney concludes a contract clause is enforceable by analogy to a precedent case. The weakener identifies a key disanalogy. One distractor strengthens the analogy; one is irrelevant.
stimulus: An attorney argues that a non-compete clause in an employment contract is legally enforceable, citing a circuit court ruling that upheld an identical clause in a contract between a financial services firm and a senior analyst. Because the clause in question is worded identically and appears in a contract between a financial services firm and a senior analyst, the attorney concludes it will be upheld by the same court.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the attorney's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Since the earlier ruling, the circuit court has issued two opinions narrowing the enforceability of non-compete clauses to situations in which the employer can demonstrate that the employee had access to genuinely proprietary trade secrets.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Non-compete clauses with identical wording have been upheld in the majority of circuit courts across the country.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The employee subject to the current clause has already accepted a position with a competing firm, making the dispute more urgent than the earlier case.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The earlier ruling was issued by a three-judge panel, which is the standard composition for circuit court decisions of that type.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The financial services industry is subject to more extensive regulatory oversight than most other sectors of the economy.

explanations.correct: The attorney's conclusion rests on the precedent from the earlier ruling. If the court has since narrowed that precedent by requiring proof of access to genuine trade secrets — a condition not established in the current case — the earlier ruling no longer straightforwardly supports enforceability, directly undermining the analogical argument.
explanations.A: Correct. Identifies a legal development that changes the controlling standard since the precedent was set, breaking the analogy between the earlier ruling and the current case.
explanations.B: Strengthens. Broader appellate support for the clause reinforces the attorney's conclusion.
explanations.C: Irrelevant. The urgency of the dispute does not affect the legal enforceability of the clause.
explanations.D: Out-of-scope. The composition of the panel is procedurally standard and irrelevant to the enforceability question.
explanations.E: Shift in subject. Industry regulatory oversight is irrelevant to the enforceability of a non-compete clause unless a connection is established — none is given here.

difficultyReason: Causal argument in arts policy concluding that public arts funding caused measurable economic benefits. The weakener attacks the direction of causation. Distractors include one strengthener and one that is irrelevant.
stimulus: A city arts commission released a report noting that neighborhoods in which municipal arts grants were concentrated over a five-year period showed, on average, a 30 percent increase in retail foot traffic and a significant rise in new business licenses compared to other neighborhoods. The commission concluded that targeted arts funding caused the economic revitalization observed in those neighborhoods.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the commission's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The city council awarded arts grants preferentially to neighborhoods that had already been identified as emerging economic hubs by a separate urban planning initiative, which itself channeled infrastructure investment into those areas.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neighborhoods that received arts grants also experienced an influx of younger residents during the same five-year period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Several of the businesses that opened in the grant-concentrated neighborhoods were arts-related, such as galleries and performance venues.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The arts commission's grant selection process was reviewed and approved by an independent auditing body.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Comparable increases in retail foot traffic were observed in similar neighborhoods in a neighboring city that implemented an identical arts-grant program over the same period.

explanations.correct: The commission concludes arts funding caused economic revitalization. If grants were directed to neighborhoods already targeted by an infrastructure investment initiative — meaning those neighborhoods were poised for economic growth regardless — the observed revitalization may be attributable to the infrastructure investment rather than the arts grants, reversing or replacing the causal direction.
explanations.A: Correct. Reveals that the grant-receiving neighborhoods were pre-selected for economic promise and received simultaneous infrastructure investment, providing an alternative (and plausibly more powerful) causal explanation for the observed economic improvements.
explanations.B: This is the 'too narrow' trap — demographic influx could be an intermediate cause or a confound, but it does not as decisively sever the causal link as A, which identifies a prior systematic selection effect.
explanations.C: Strengthens, or at minimum is consistent with the causal claim — arts-related businesses opening in arts-grant neighborhoods supports the conclusion that arts funding drove economic activity.
explanations.D: Irrelevant. The auditing of the grant process does not bear on whether the grants caused economic revitalization.
explanations.E: Strengthens. Replication of the result in a comparable city under identical conditions supports the causal inference.
